# Editable GIS handover

This contribution extends the original Upper Savannah scientific Workspace with
complete, portable desktop GIS projects. It exports retained source editions,
prepared grids, completed baseline and alternative runs, and signed comparison
rasters without rerunning the scientific models. Every physical raster keeps its
original cells, mask, coordinate system and companions. Legends and overviews apply
the declared band scale and offset, matching the QGIS provider; raw and physical
extrema are both retained. The provider behavior is documented in its source:
https://api.qgis.org/api/3.44/qgsrasterdataprovider_8cpp_source.html Every vector working copy
is a GeoPackage containing the full selected geometry and attributes.


## Continue a completed map delivery in Editable GIS

Open the completed delivery in **Maps and delivery**, then choose **Prepare editable GIS project**. The existing Editable GIS desk opens with that exact delivery selected, the original study coordinate system, and its actual retained GIS datasets. The same delivery can be selected directly in the desk's **Completed map delivery** field.

The completed-delivery selection includes baseline physical exports, every retained signed scenario difference, and the actual generic, receptor or receiving-water priorities used in the atlas. The model-domain and reporting-area polygons become separate editable context layers. Dataset source identities, units, original masks and numerical values remain attached to the existing scientific result.

Starting from a delivery deliberately starts with its own datasets. Other source editions, prepared grids, runs or comparisons can be added explicitly in the existing form. The delivery ID is saved with that Workspace's form; catalogue refresh preserves both the selected delivery and edits made while the request is in flight. The original source-only intake remains available.

Click **Build complete GIS project**. This submits the normal gis.project.export task. Open its original task result and download the complete editable ZIP. The existing OPEN_GIS.html and project.qgz entry points, independent receive operation and seal/pack workflow apply to this project.

### Original atlas relationships and working layers

Each retained delivery dataset becomes one logical GIS layer. A priority raster serving multiple map families stays one layer with every original map relationship. Distinct comparison artifacts retain their distinct original dataset and scenario identities even when the numerical TIFF bytes match.

Physical exports and signed differences retain the engine's original metric/units/purpose style grouping. Signed differences retain alternative-minus-baseline direction and common valid support. Dimensionless priorities carry their own normalization and geographic-support identity, so unrelated priority methods do not acquire a shared scientific metric merely because they have the same units.

Completed atlas layers retain their original saved display limits, units, percentile method and map relationships. The original map renderer’s Greys palette applies to physical exports and priorities; its RdBu_r palette applies to signed alternative-minus-baseline changes. Other source/run exports keep the existing shared full-native-cell grayscale policy. The original map display_scale remains in each layer’s retained source metadata.

Every layer.source retains the complete original dataset record: grid and profile IDs, baseline and alternative run/scenario records, producing-model provenance, source editions, original comparison identity, physical header, support method, derivation and atlas map relationships.

### Metadata, maps and report context

One context attachment preserves the original delivery-relative directory hierarchy. It contains the existing atlas PDF, JSON/CSV index, source context, individual map PDFs, dataset GeoTIFFs and actual companions, FGDC XML, native/grid provenance, display-scale metadata and self-contained scientific PDF reports. The FGDC links from gis/metadata to the actual original dataset paths continue to resolve after independent receiving.

Open the attachment from OPEN_GIS.html. Its files retain their original bytes and names. The separate working layers are independent copies intended for desktop editing; the attached originals remain the immutable source context for the edited edition.

The source binding also records the original delivery-state descriptor and its scientific/complete archive descriptors as lineage. The map-and-dataset attachment contains the explicit GIS/report members described above. Use the original completed delivery's archive controls when the full scientific Workspace is needed.

A completed delivery must have the current upstate.atlas-datasets/v1 catalogue. Older delivery editions remain visible with their reason; build the current edition from their retained scientific selections to provide the exact dataset relationships. The queued export verifies the complete record, atlas/dataset agreement and every selected member before invoking the maintained GIS builder.

### Command-line selection

The original command remains:

~~~sh
python model/gis_project_cli.py workspace-export "$WORKSPACE" delivery-gis-selection.json
~~~

The selection JSON includes the actual delivery_id, a project title and optional display CRS:

~~~json
{
  "title": "Selected completed watershed delivery",
  "delivery_id": "ACTUAL_64_CHARACTER_DELIVERY_ID",
  "sources": [],
  "notes": ["Editable GIS handover of the retained map delivery."]
}
~~~

Omitting project_crs selects the original delivery grid CRS. An explicitly supplied project_crs changes the project's display coordinates through the existing builder while preserving each working dataset's native coordinates.

The same request/result identities, complete GIS inventory, QGS/QGZ references, original file transport, desktop edit sealing and received-source adoption govern this continuation. Its operation is ES-20261013-DELIVERY-GIS-PROJECT; source is contained in the existing gis_workspace, GIS desk and delivery inspector paths.


## Review the actual changes in a received GIS edition

In **Editable GIS projects**, open the received edition's **Compare exported and received working editions** section. Select the retained **Original exported GIS project** and choose **Build complete edition comparison**. Only exports with the same original GIS selection are offered. The queued operation verifies the actual original request, both inventory fingerprints, logical layer IDs, retained source identities and complete working files.

This comparison uses the original exported working data and the actual received working data. The existing **Working vector changes** control separately compares received vectors with their original retained source features; its original-source/Fiona identity reference remains available. Choose the comparison whose original reference matches the question. The received edition's seal history remains available as additional provenance; a file-hash history alone does not supply the old geometry or raster values.

The normal task result opens the completed report and its full ZIP, JSON and layer-summary CSV. The received card retains the exact original export choice through refresh and displays completed reviews with their actual edition identities and report creation time. Changing the selected original export clears an incompatible optional adoption review, while preserving the separate adoption title, reason, working-layer and original table/document choices.

### What the report contains

Vector layers are paired using their original collision-safe source identity field, without converting identifiers such as 001 into numbers. The comparison streams complete properties and geometries through a disk-backed index. It distinguishes typed attribute changes, coordinate changes, topologically equivalent geometry, added and removed features, and missing or duplicate identities. Ambiguous rows are retained as individual unpaired records. They are not silently overwritten or matched by row position.

Each vector layer has a complete changes.jsonl file with original and received properties and geometry for every changed or unpaired row, plus a compact changes.csv. Only a small example set enters the report summary; the full change records remain downloadable. Header/schema and CRS changes are retained even when ordinary attribute values are unchanged. A changed CRS leaves geometric comparison unpaired while the exact original coordinates and attributes remain in the records.

Raster review concerns the original logical GIS layer's selected band. The complete before/after all-band header, data types, nodata, scale, offset, descriptions, mask flags and units remain in the report. Native cells are paired only when the actual CRS, dimensions, six affine values and selected band agree. A changed grid is reported as an unpaired structural change; it is not resampled to manufacture cell comparisons.

On a matching grid, 512-by-512 windows retain counts for common finite-valid cells, added/removed valid support, neither-valid cells and nonfinite unmasked values. The support-change.tif codes are:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Neither edition has a finite-valid selected-band value |
| 1 | Both editions have a finite-valid selected-band value |
| 2 | The received edition adds a finite-valid value |
| 3 | The received edition removes a finite-valid value |

The value-change.tif is **received minus exported**, in the original declared physical units, on common support. Raw encoding changes are counted separately. The comparison applies each original band scale and offset, cancels equal offsets before subtraction, and uses exact scalar input arithmetic when large integers or changed encoding parameters require it. Float64 output cannot represent every mathematically possible difference; such cells have an explicit unrepresentable count and NoData instead of a misleading zero. Exact change counts and the retained native input editions remain available. Summary mean and RMSE concern the representable difference cells.

Categorical layers and layers with different declared units retain raw-change and support counts without assigning an arithmetic physical difference across categories or different units. Working-file and actual companion changes remain separate from the selected-band numeric result; the report does not describe other bands as numerically unchanged.

### Portable report and recovery

The complete review ZIP opens through **REVIEW.html** and includes both original project manifests, review.json, layers.csv and every layer's full change records or derived support/value rasters. The report preserves the exact exported/received project and edition IDs, original source/run/scenario provenance, inventory fingerprints and subtraction direction. Keep the complete ZIP contents together so its relative links resolve.

Review output is retained under:

~~~text
gis-received/<receipt_id>/reviews/<review_id>/
~~~

The received project and its inventory remain immutable. A failed operation continues from completed layer checkpoints whose native files and companions were checked against the original input inventory. A changed-input failure invalidates the affected attempt's reusable checkpoints. Completion rechecks the complete original input fingerprints before retaining its final report.

The normal full scientific Workspace backup and restore carry the received project, original export and review together. The portable review ZIP supplies the change report and its data; the complete GIS project ZIP supplies the independently editable original/received working layers.

### Retain a review with an adopted source edition

In the existing received-source adoption form, **Retain a change review with this source edition** is an explicit choice. It offers complete reviews matching the selected original export and the exact current received fingerprint. Selecting a review retains its complete report context with the new original source collection and makes that review identity part of the adoption selection.

The original adoption path also supports received working layers or selected original tables and documents without attaching a review. Working-layer selections still retain all required original attachments. Independent table/document selection, native types, units, dates, geography, companions and original queued-task recovery stay available.

The full application CLI uses the same backend:

~~~sh
python model/gis_project_cli.py workspace-review "$WORKSPACE" gis-review-selection.json
~~~

A selection file contains actual retained IDs:

~~~json
{
  "receipt_id": "ACTUAL_RECEIVED_GIS_ID",
  "export_id": "ACTUAL_ORIGINAL_EXPORTED_GIS_ID"
}
~~~

For optional reviewed adoption, add the actual review_id to the existing workspace-adopt-sources selection. Omit that field for the original adoption path. Standalone GIS seal/pack/receive tools remain usable independently; Workspace review uses the installed scientific application's gis_edition_review module.

Operation: ES-20261013-RECEIVED-GIS-REVIEW.

## Open and continue a delivery

Extract the complete archive into a new directory. Open **OPEN_GIS.html** for the
self-contained geographic overviews, layer search, units, run/source identities,
and operating instructions. Open **project.qgz** in QGIS for the editable layers.
Keep the whole directory together: QGIS project files refer to the accompanying
data using relative paths. The QGIS file-format documentation describes these
project/data relationships: https://docs.qgis.org/3.44/en/docs/user_manual/appendices/qgis_file_formats.html

The `originals/` directory preserves the selected source bytes and companions.
The `layers/` directory contains independent working copies, not hardlinks. A
vector's `source_row_id` (or collision-safe equivalent declared in the metadata)
maps the working row to its original row. `layers.csv` is the complete layer table;
`project.json` retains the selection, units, case identities, methods and history.
Raster overviews use nearest-cell display resampling. Vector overviews use
explicitly recorded topology-preserving simplification. Neither replaces the
full-resolution numerical or geometric data.

After editing attributes, geometries or styling, save inside the received directory
and close editing before recording the edition:

```sh
python tools/model/gis_project_cli.py seal . --reason "Reviewed catchment attributes"
python tools/model/gis_project_cli.py pack . ../reviewed-gis.zip
python tools/model/gis_project_cli.py receive ../reviewed-gis.zip ../next-receiver
```

When both project files changed, select `--project-file project.qgz` or
`--project-file project.qgs`. The selected native project is synchronized to the
other format. Existing layer IDs and relative working paths remain fixed; added
external datasets or reprojected vector sources enter through a new explicit
selection. The next receiver can edit and transfer again. The sender's retained
originals are not modified. Metadata history retains previous inventories and
manifests; retain a prior ZIP to preserve that edition's complete working bytes.

## Use the maintained scientific Workspace

Run from the original product root, with its original `model/workspace.py` and GIS
dependencies installed:

```sh
python -m model.gis_project_cli workspace-catalogue /path/to/study
python -m model.gis_project_cli workspace-export /path/to/study selection.json
```

A source-only selection is useful before native model execution:

```json
{
  "title": "Upper Savannah retained study geography",
  "project_crs": "EPSG:5070",
  "source_collection_id": "ACTUAL_RETAINED_COLLECTION_ID",
  "sources": [
    {"source_id": "ACTUAL_RETAINED_DOMAIN_ID", "visible": true},
    {"source_id": "ACTUAL_RETAINED_REPORTING_ID", "visible": true}
  ]
}
```

The IDs above are explicit placeholders, not invented study data. Obtain the
actual IDs from `workspace-catalogue`. Include `grid_id` and `include_grid: true`
for the original prepared grid; `baseline_run_id`, `scenario_run_ids` and
`comparison_ids` select existing complete outputs. A source collection without a
`sources` list selects all its retained entries. Each selected source can specify
an original vector `layer`, an equality `where` object, `units`, `purpose`, `group`
and initial `visible` state. `purpose` distinguishes context, categorical,
physical, priority and difference layers.

The adapter uses the original `source_file`, `get_grid`, `inspect_run`, `_get` and
source-catalogue interfaces. It retains the original run/profile/scenario IDs and
actual declared artifact units. It does not substitute an ecological model or
create new run outputs. Export results live under
`WORKSPACE/gis-exports/SELECTION_HASH/` with the project directory, complete archive,
selection and export record. Same-request reopening verifies the retained edition.

## Build from retained files directly

The direct CLI needs no scientific Workspace installation:

```sh
python model/gis_project_cli.py build request.json output-directory --source-root retained-inputs
python model/gis_project_cli.py verify output-directory
python model/gis_project_cli.py pack output-directory complete-gis.zip
```

A request uses schema `upstate.gis-request/v1`, title, project CRS and a nonempty
`layers` array. Every layer declares `id`, `title`, `kind` (`vector` or `raster`),
`file` (`path`, exact `bytes`, SHA-256), optional `companions`, `group`, `units`,
`purpose`, source provenance and selection options. Paths are relative to the
explicit source root. GeoTIFFs retain all dependencies, including masks. An
original `.json.gz` vector is read through GDAL's gzip driver. Other original
files are carried as attachments, with complete companion sets.

The full request used in the included county operating case is retained in its
processing-source archive. Its named county source is Basemap's installed
UScounties dataset; three state selections contain 305 complete county features.
Two 30 m geographic rasters derive from the Anderson/Oconee/Pickens county union.
The county mask and Euclidean boundary distance are explicitly described
geographic processing examples, not the official HUC12 domain or pollutant results.
Original data notices and processing methods accompany that case.

## Native QGIS receiving

Use the Python environment supplied with an installed QGIS 3 application. The
helper requires QGIS bindings but does not invoke InVEST:

```sh
QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen /usr/bin/python3 tools/model/gis_project_native.py \
  original-project new-native-receiver
```

It copies the **complete package** to the new receiving directory, opens every
layer with QGIS, checks provider validity and populations/dimensions, renders the
selected map, saves QGIS's own project, reopens it, and writes the resulting
version/provider information and image into that received package. The sender
stays unchanged. An unsuccessful opening leaves its copied directory available
for diagnosis and produces no successful native-receiving record.

The authored cloud execution used Python 3.13, Fiona 1.10.1, Rasterio 1.5.0,
pyproj 3.7.2, Shapely 2.1.2 and Chromium. Full data export, receiving, recipient
editing and second receiving ran there. QGIS Python was not installed in that
container; its native-desktop helper therefore requires the equipped receiving
host. Browser interaction checks rendered the actual self-contained HTML in
Chromium; administrator policy prevented network/file navigation in that browser.

## Operating sequence for Bryce

**Inspect.** Open the delivered HTML. Choose a layer, inspect its units and source
identity, then use *Fit selected layer*. Explain: “Each layer identifies its source
and case, so the map can be traced to the underlying data.”

**Compare.** Toggle the selected baseline and alternative groups. Matching physical
metrics and units use a common legend range. Signed difference layers retain the
original comparison direction; dimensionless priorities are not pollutant loads.
Explain: “The comparison preserves the native units and tells us which case and
parameter profile produced the result.”

**Work.** Open `project.qgz`, expand a case group and inspect a raster value or the
GeoPackage's attribute table. Explain: “This is an editable GIS project. The
operator receives the data, source files and project structure.”

**Return.** Edit a working attribute, save and close it, seal with the reason, then
pack and receive into a different directory. Explain: “The recipient can continue
independently; we retain the original data and identify each transferred edition.”

## Implementation boundaries

All exports use create-only staged publication. Hash inventories cover every
retained file, copied original and history record. ZIP receiving checks paths,
member collisions, available space and extracted identities before publishing the
new directory. Packing verifies the bytes it actually writes. The kernel releases
process locks after interruption; the next operation can retry the same request.
These checks belong to file correctness, not a new business approval policy.

This component owns only the additive GIS files. Installation into the original
operator's queue/navigation/download system must compose the current owning
source instead of overwriting another agent's operator panels. The CLI and Python
adapter are the direct maintained entrypoints of this source edition.

## Original operator integration

The contribution includes the complete grayscale `Editable GIS projects` panel,
queued `gis.project.export`, `gis.project.receive`, `gis.project.adopt-sources`,
`gis.project.review` and `gis.vector.review` operations, original upload
receiving, independent archive copies and the original hash-checked downloads.

Apply the component installer to the current complete application. It uses the
receiving application's maintained extension installer when present; the original
pre-registry application retains its narrow direct integration:

```sh
python install_gis_projects.py --application /path/to/original/application --dry-run
python install_gis_projects.py --application /path/to/original/application
```

The installer composes the actual registration source, preserves unrelated
source, validates Python syntax before mutation, checks source predecessors and
retains exact before-images. On a registry application it calls the installed
`install_extensions.py` source transformations and registers the complete
`gis-projects` and `gis-vector-reviews` descriptors and their source files. It removes the exact former GIS-owned direct hooks when
migrating an older GIS installation, so the shared registry owns the actions,
navigation, assets and file routes once. Reapplying the same edition makes no
changes.

Both review references are installed together. The `gis-projects` provider
compares an exported working edition with the received edition; the separate
`gis-vector-reviews` provider compares original source features with their
received working features. The installer carries their original model modules,
providers and descriptors. On a pre-registry application, it upgrades an existing
GIS installation with the original vector action, authorized catalogue/inspect
routes, retained-item lookup and task decoration. Reapplying keeps those hooks
single; migration to the shared registry removes their exact former direct joins
before the descriptors become the active owners. The application's existing
authorization, Workspace selection, queue, download tickets and file policies
remain the same.

Start
the original `operator/server.py` with its original startup command, then select
**Editable GIS projects**. Choose an actual source edition, prepared grid and/or
completed cases. Click **Build complete GIS project**, inspect the original task,
and download its complete archive. The **Receive independent edition** form uses
the original uploader and keeps the received GIS separate from the study engine.

For ECSA's shared registry, `operator/extensions/gis-projects.json` implements the
actual published `upstate.operator-extension/v1` descriptor. It uses the same
backend implementation and lifecycle, not a second queue. The client requests the
original `getState`, `api`, `refreshState`, `showTask` and `toast` callbacks.
The component installer selects the current application's host automatically and
keeps one navigation and task owner. It composes the installed host source in
memory before writing the completed change; it never replaces that host with the
older GIS-era server, browser or registry.

### Inspect the exact outgoing populated product

The application-level **AGENTS.md** retains the owner's rendered-product
instruction, version **2026-10-13.1**. The component installer carries the current
source copy into the receiving application and preserves its existing local
instructions. Reapplication updates only the installer's marked instruction
section when one is present; its ordinary before-image journal retains the
previous bytes.

Before describing the outgoing GIS application, change report or handover as
ready, the producing worker must run and open that exact outgoing version, look
at its rendered screens or actual screenshots, and operate the important controls.
Use the existing populated county/study Workspace and its retained export,
received edition and review IDs. Inspect the actual screenshare width and a
narrow/mobile width, with relevant populated, empty, loading and error states.

In the existing GIS desk, inspect both comparison references, the selected
original export/received edition, the complete layer report, explicit unpaired
or skipped-arithmetic explanations, and the optional review context for source
adoption. Open the actual **REVIEW.html** and its downloads; extract the complete
report ZIP and follow its relative files after reopening. Inspect the corresponding

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Capture original WBD topology and geometry for the reviewed Upper Savannah basin."""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse, collections, gzip, hashlib, json, os, pathlib, shutil, tempfile
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from urllib.parse import urlencode
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen
from urllib.error import HTTPError

BASE = "https://hydro.nationalmap.gov/arcgis/rest/services/wbd/MapServer/6"
HUC8 = ("03060101", "03060102", "03060103", "03060106", "03060107")
PLANNING_SHA = "133bc5369bd0d68bfdb53c61e3df24f9445f799b0d68b301f321d2c49d71eab6"
LIMIT = 64 * 1024 * 1024

def now():
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()

def digest(value):
    return hashlib.sha256(value).hexdigest()

def encode(value):
    return (json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n").encode()

def exact_write(path, body):
    path = pathlib.Path(path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if path.exists():
        if path.read_bytes() != body:
            raise ValueError("Retained file has another identity: " + str(path))
        return
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=".source-publish-", dir=path.parent) as temporary:
        staged = pathlib.Path(temporary) / "file"
        with staged.open("xb") as output:
            output.write(body); output.flush(); os.fsync(output.fileno())
        try:
            os.link(staged, path)
        except FileExistsError:
            if path.read_bytes() != body:
                raise
        fd = os.open(path.parent, os.O_RDONLY)
        try: os.fsync(fd)
        finally: os.close(fd)

class Capture:
    def __init__(self, root):
        self.root = pathlib.Path(root).absolute()
        self.root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.responses = {}

    def get(self, name, parameters):
        url = BASE + "/query?" + urlencode({"f": "json", **parameters})
        folder = self.root / "responses" / name
        receipt_path = folder / "receipt.json"
        if receipt_path.exists():
            receipt = json.loads(receipt_path.read_bytes())
            if receipt["requested_url"] != url:
                raise ValueError("The retained response belongs to another exact query.")
            stored = (folder / "body.json.gz").read_bytes()
            body = gzip.decompress(stored)
            if (digest(stored) != receipt["stored_sha256"]
                    or len(stored) != receipt["stored_bytes"]
                    or digest(body) != receipt["sha256"]
                    or len(body) != receipt["bytes"]):
                raise ValueError("A retained original response changed.")
        else:
            requested_at = now()
            request = Request(url, headers={"Accept": "application/json", "Accept-Encoding": "identity",
                                          "User-Agent": "TJLabs Upper Savannah source research"})
            try:
                response = urlopen(request, timeout=60)
            except HTTPError as error:
                response = error
            with response:
                wire = response.read(LIMIT + 1)
                if len(wire) > LIMIT:
                    raise ValueError("The original response exceeds the declared 64 MiB response allowance.")
                headers = dict(response.headers.items())
                content_encoding = response.headers.get("Content-Encoding", "identity").lower()
                if content_encoding not in ("identity", "gzip"):
                    raise ValueError("The provider returned an unsupported explicit content encoding.")
                body = gzip.decompress(wire) if content_encoding == "gzip" else wire
                if len(body) > LIMIT:
                    raise ValueError("The decoded original response exceeds 64 MiB.")
                stored = gzip.compress(body, mtime=0)
                receipt = {"requested_url": url, "response_url": response.geturl(),
                           "status": response.status, "headers": headers,
                           "requested_at": requested_at, "captured_at": now(),
                           "bytes": len(body), "sha256": digest(body),
                           "stored_bytes": len(stored), "stored_sha256": digest(stored),
                           "storage_encoding": "gzip", "content_encoding": content_encoding,
                           "wire_bytes": len(wire), "wire_sha256": digest(wire)}
            parent = folder.parent
            parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="." + name + "-", dir=parent) as temporary:
                staged = pathlib.Path(temporary) / "response"
                staged.mkdir()
                exact_write(staged / "body.json.gz", stored)
                if wire != body:
                    exact_write(staged / "wire.bin", wire)
                    receipt["wire_file"] = "wire.bin"
                exact_write(staged / "receipt.json", encode(receipt))
                try:
                    os.rename(staged, folder)
                except FileExistsError:
                    raise ValueError("Another source capture published this query. Reopen its retained response.")
            print(json.dumps({"captured": name, "status": receipt["status"],
                              "bytes": receipt["bytes"], "stored_bytes": receipt["stored_bytes"]}), flush=True)
        self.responses[name] = {"folder": folder.relative_to(self.root).as_posix(), **receipt}
        if receipt["status"] != 200:
            raise ValueError("Original provider status " + str(receipt["status"]) + " retained at " + str(folder))
        value = json.loads(body)
        if "error" in value:
            raise ValueError("Original provider error retained at " + str(folder) + ": " + json.dumps(value["error"]))
        if value.get("exceededTransferLimit"):
            raise ValueError("The provider truncated this exact response; its original body is retained.")
        return value

def pages(values, size):
    values = list(values)
    for start in range(0, len(values), size):
        yield values[start:start + size]

def esri_polygon(geometry, corrections, identity):
    from shapely.geometry import Polygon, GeometryCollection
    from shapely import make_valid, is_valid_reason
    if not geometry or "curveRings" in geometry or "rings" not in geometry:
        raise ValueError("Preserve and resolve the original non-linear or absent geometry for " + identity)
    combined = GeometryCollection()
    for ring in geometry["rings"]:
        polygon = Polygon(ring)
        if not polygon.is_valid:
            corrections.append({"identity": identity, "stage": "ring", "reason": is_valid_reason(polygon),
                                "analysis_operation": "Shapely make_valid; original response geometry unchanged"})
            polygon = make_valid(polygon)
        combined = combined.symmetric_difference(polygon)
    if not combined.is_valid:
        corrections.append({"identity": identity, "stage": "assembled", "reason": is_valid_reason(combined),
                            "analysis_operation": "Shapely make_valid; original response geometry unchanged"})
        combined = make_valid(combined)
    return combined

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--planning-source", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--reference-wbd-source", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    capture = Capture(args.output)
    output = capture.root
    completed = output / "capture.json"
    if completed.exists():
        retained = json.loads(completed.read_bytes())
        if retained.get("schema") != "upstate.wbd-network-capture/v1":
            raise ValueError("This output belongs to another source capture.")
        for item in retained["files"]:
            body = (output / item["path"]).read_bytes()
            if len(body) != item["bytes"] or digest(body) != item["sha256"]:
                raise ValueError("A completed native capture member changed: " + item["path"])
        print(json.dumps({"complete": True, "reused": True, "source_root": str(output),
                          "manifest_sha256": digest(completed.read_bytes()),
                          "retained_bytes": retained["retained_bytes"]}), flush=True)
        return
    planning = pathlib.Path(args.planning_source).absolute()
    reference = pathlib.Path(args.reference_wbd_source).absolute()
    original_shp = (planning / "PlanningBasins2023.shp").read_bytes()
    if digest(original_shp) != PLANNING_SHA:
        raise ValueError("Use the retained original PlanningBasins2023 shapefile.")
    import shapefile, pyproj
    from shapely.geometry import shape
    from shapely.ops import transform
    reader = shapefile.Reader(str(planning / "PlanningBasins2023.shp"))
    selected = [(index + 1, record) for index, record in enumerate(reader.iterShapeRecords())
                if record.record.as_dict().get("Basin") == "Upper Savannah"]
    if len(selected) != 1 or selected[0][0] != 5:
        raise ValueError("The original source must select exactly Upper Savannah native record 5.")
    reporting = shape(selected[0][1].shape.__geo_interface__)
    planning_crs = pyproj.CRS.from_wkt((planning / "PlanningBasins2023.prj").read_text())
    layer_raw = gzip.decompress((reference / "layer-6.json.gz").read_bytes())
    layer = json.loads(layer_raw)
    fields = {f["name"].lower(): f["name"] for f in layer["fields"]}
    oid = next(f["name"] for f in layer["fields"] if f["type"] == "esriFieldTypeOID")
    huc, downstream = fields["huc12"], fields["tohuc"]
    source_crs = layer["extent"]["spatialReference"]
    wkid = source_crs.get("latestWkid") or source_crs["wkid"]
    projection = pyproj.Transformer.from_crs(pyproj.CRS.from_epsg(wkid), planning_crs, always_xy=True).transform
    exact_write(output / "reference" / "layer-6.json.gz", (reference / "layer-6.json.gz").read_bytes())
    reference_manifest = json.loads((reference / "capture.json").read_bytes())
    layer_receipt = next(r for r in reference_manifest["responses"] if r["file"] == "layer-6.json.gz")
    exact_write(output / "reference" / "layer-6.receipt.json", encode(layer_receipt))
    where = huc + " LIKE '030601%'"
    count = capture.get("savannah-count", {"where": where, "returnCountOnly": "true"})["count"]
    id_response = capture.get("savannah-ids", {"where": where, "returnIdsOnly": "true"})
    ids = sorted(id_response["objectIds"])
    if len(ids) != count or len(set(ids)) != len(ids):
        raise ValueError("Native count and complete unique object-ID response differ.")
    attributes, by_huc = {}, {}
    def add_attributes(requested, name):
        result = capture.get(name, {"objectIds": ",".join(map(str, requested)),
                                  "outFields": "*", "returnGeometry": "false"})
        records = result["features"]
        if {f["attributes"][oid] for f in records} != set(requested) or len(records) != len(requested):
            raise ValueError("The original attribute page does not contain its exact requested ID set.")
        for feature in records:
            row = feature["attributes"]; key = str(row[huc])
            if row[oid] in attributes and attributes[row[oid]] != row:
                raise ValueError("The same original object ID has two attribute editions in this capture.")
            if key in by_huc and by_huc[key] != row[oid]:
                raise ValueError("The native HUC12 identity is not unique.")
            attributes[row[oid]] = row; by_huc[key] = row[oid]
    for index, group in enumerate(pages(ids, 1000)):
        add_attributes(group, "savannah-attributes-%04d" % index)
    geometry_locations, projected, source_geometry = {}, {}, {}
    corrections = []
    focus_path = reference / "selected-four-huc12.json.gz"
    if focus_path.exists():
        original_focus = json.loads(gzip.decompress(focus_path.read_bytes()))
        focus_receipt = next(r for r in reference_manifest["responses"] if r["file"] == focus_path.name)
        reusable = [f for f in original_focus["features"]
                    if attributes.get(f["attributes"][oid]) == f["attributes"]]
        if reusable:
            exact_write(output / "reference" / focus_path.name, focus_path.read_bytes())
            exact_write(output / "reference" / "selected-four-huc12.receipt.json", encode(focus_receipt))
        for index, feature in enumerate(original_focus["features"]):
            row = feature["attributes"]; identity = row[oid]
            if attributes.get(identity) != row: continue
            geometry = esri_polygon(feature["geometry"], corrections, str(row[huc]))
            source_geometry[identity] = geometry
            projected[identity] = transform(projection, geometry)
            geometry_locations[identity] = {"file": "reference/" + focus_path.name,
                                            "feature_index": index, "captured_at": focus_receipt["captured_at"],
                                            "reused_original_response": True}
    def acquire_geometry(requested, label):
        missing = sorted(set(requested) - set(geometry_locations))
        for index, group in enumerate(pages(missing, 50)):
            name = label + "-%04d" % index
            result = capture.get(name, {"objectIds": ",".join(map(str, group)), "outFields": "*",
                                       "returnGeometry": "true", "returnTrueCurves": "true"})
            rows = result["features"]
            if {f["attributes"][oid] for f in rows} != set(group) or len(rows) != len(group):
                raise ValueError("The native geometry page does not contain exactly its requested IDs.")
            spatial = result.get("spatialReference", source_crs)
            if (spatial.get("latestWkid") or spatial.get("wkid")) != wkid:
                raise ValueError("The source geometry CRS changed between its native contract and response.")
            for position, feature in enumerate(rows):
                row = feature["attributes"]; identity = row[oid]
                if attributes[identity] != row:
                    raise ValueError("Original attributes changed between topology and geometry acquisition; both responses are retained.")
                geometry = esri_polygon(feature["geometry"], corrections, str(row[huc]))
                source_geometry[identity] = geometry
                projected[identity] = transform(projection, geometry)
                geometry_locations[identity] = {"file": "responses/" + name + "/body.json.gz",
                                               "feature_index": position,
                                               "captured_at": capture.responses[name]["captured_at"]}
    candidate_ids = [identity for identity, row in attributes.items() if str(row[huc])[:8] in HUC8]
    acquire_geometry(candidate_ids, "reporting-context-geometry")
    intersections = {str(attributes[i][huc]): projected[i].intersection(reporting).area
                     for i in candidate_ids if projected[i].intersects(reporting)}
    intersections = {key: value for key, value in intersections.items() if value > 0}
    if not intersections:
        raise ValueError("The reviewed basin did not intersect its published HUC12 context.")
    def closure():
        reverse = collections.defaultdict(list)
        for row in attributes.values():
            reverse[str(row[downstream])].append(str(row[huc]))
        selected, frontier = set(intersections), list(intersections)
        while frontier:
            key = frontier.pop()
            for ancestor in reverse.get(key, ()):
                if ancestor not in selected: selected.add(ancestor); frontier.append(ancestor)
        return selected
    selected_hucs, checked_external = closure(), set()
    # Retain a provider check for incoming edges outside the named Savannah HUC6.
    # New external ancestors, if present, become ordinary source rows and are followed.
    while selected_hucs - checked_external:
        frontier = sorted(selected_hucs - checked_external)
        for group in pages(frontier, 80):
            selection = downstream + " IN (" + ",".join("'" + key + "'" for key in group) + ")"
            selection += " AND " + huc + " NOT LIKE '030601%'"
            token = digest(selection.encode())[:20]
            result = capture.get("outside-incoming-ids-" + token,
                                 {"where": selection, "returnIdsOnly": "true"})
            outside = sorted(set(result.get("objectIds") or []) - set(attributes))
            for index, incoming in enumerate(pages(outside, 1000)):
                add_attributes(incoming, "outside-attributes-" + token + "-%04d" % index)
            checked_external.update(group)
        selected_hucs = closure()
    selected_ids = [by_huc[key] for key in sorted(selected_hucs)]
    acquire_geometry(selected_ids, "upstream-ancestor-geometry")
    records = []
    for key in sorted(selected_hucs):
        identity = by_huc[key]; row = attributes[identity]
        records.append({"huc12": key, "object_id": identity, "tohuc": str(row[downstream]),
                        "reporting_intersection_m2": intersections.get(key, 0),
                        "intersects_reporting_area": key in intersections,
                        "upstream_ancestor": key not in intersections,
                        "geometry": geometry_locations[identity]})
    source_rows = [{"object_id": identity, "attributes": attributes[identity]}
                   for identity in sorted(attributes)]
    exact_write(output / "topology-records.json", encode({"schema": "upstate.wbd-topology-records/v1",
                "object_id_field": oid, "huc12_field": huc, "tohuc_field": downstream,
                "records": source_rows}))
    selection = {"schema": "upstate.wbd-upstream-selection/v1",
                 "reporting_source": {"edition": "PlanningBasins2023", "shapefile_sha256": PLANNING_SHA,

The ten complete counties sum to 1,659,022 persons in July 2025, up 147,105 (9.73%) from their same-vintage April 2020 estimates base. These are whole-county demographic context totals. Watershed-level population needs a spatial allocation dataset and method; a county boundary overlap by itself does not determine that allocation.

"""Receive selected originals through the installed Operator queue and downloads."""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
import sys
import time
import zipfile


def file_sha(path):
    value = hashlib.sha256()
    with Path(path).open("rb") as stream:
        for block in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
            value.update(block)
    return value.hexdigest()


def run(application, workspace, state_directory, selected_refs=None, timeout=180,
        require_declared_companions=False):
    application, workspace = Path(application).resolve(), Path(workspace).resolve()
    state_directory = Path(state_directory).resolve()

    from intelligence import IntelligenceFeature
    from eco_intelligence.adapters import CatalogRepository
    from science_catalog_delivery import bundle, verify_delivery

    def complete(operator, task):
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
        while task["state"] in {"queued", "running"}:
            if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                raise TimeoutError("Original task still active: " + task["id"])
            time.sleep(0.1)
            task = operator.task(task["id"])
        if task["state"] != "complete":
            raise RuntimeError(json.dumps(task, ensure_ascii=False))
        return task

    def controller(operator):
        if not operator.extensions.handles_action("intelligence.collection.export"):
            raise RuntimeError("Receive the current registry and selected-source overlay in this application.")

                    member = body.get("view_path", body["filename"])

                               if (candidate.get("metadata") or {}).get("source_binding") == {
                                   "collection_id": binding["collection_id"],
                                   "source_id": binding["source_id"],
                                   "member": member, "role": "companion"}]
                    if len(matches) != 1:
                        raise AssertionError("An original declared companion has no unique native binding.")
                    companion = matches[0]
                    path = Path(companion["path"])
                    path = (path if path.is_absolute() else workspace / path).resolve()
                    expected_companions.append({
                        "primary_id": ref["id"], "source_dataset_id": companion["id"],
                        "member": member, "path": path.relative_to(workspace).as_posix(),
                        "bytes": body["bytes"], "sha256": body["sha256"],
                    })
            selection["expected_companions"] = expected_companions
            selection_path.write_text(json.dumps(selection, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n",
                                      encoding="utf-8")
        expected_companions = selection["expected_companions"]
        if require_declared_companions and not expected_companions:
            raise ValueError("Select an actual retained source primary with declared companions in this Workspace.")

        creation_body = {"title": "Original source collection receiving"}
        create_op = "eco264b_original_collection_create"
        creation = complete(operator, operator.submit(
            key, "intelligence.session.create", creation_body, create_op))
        sid = creation["result"]["session_id"]
        payload = {"session_id": sid, "title": "Original scientific source collection", "refs": refs}
        export_op = "eco264b_original_collection_export"
        exported = complete(operator, operator.submit(
            key, "intelligence.collection.export", payload, export_op))
        replay = operator.submit(key, "intelligence.collection.export", payload, export_op)
        if replay["id"] != exported["id"]:
            raise AssertionError("The original operation produced another task.")

        original_view = feature.read(key, "collection", {
            "session_id": sid, "collection_id": collection_id})
        ticket = next(item for item in original_view["files"] if item["format"] == "zip")
        archive_path = state_directory / "original-source-collection.zip"
        original_file, item = operator.open_download(ticket["id"])
        try:
            with archive_path.open("wb") as output:
                for block in iter(lambda: original_file.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
                    output.write(block)

            original_file.close()
        if archive_path.stat().st_size != ticket["bytes"] or file_sha(archive_path) != ticket["sha256"]:
            raise AssertionError("The downloaded archive differs from the original native ticket.")
    finally:
        operator.close()

    extracted = state_directory / "received-original-collection"
    extracted.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(archive_path) as archive:
        for member in archive.infolist():
            path = PurePosixPath(member.filename)
            if path.is_absolute() or ".." in path.parts or "\\" in member.filename:
                raise ValueError("Unexpected archive member.")
        archive.extractall(extracted)
    received = verify_delivery(extracted)
    if not (extracted / "START.html").is_file():
        raise AssertionError("The original-file browser was not included.")
    catalog = json.loads((extracted / "catalog.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    repository = CatalogRepository(extracted / "catalog.json", extracted)
    original_tenant = next(iter(catalog["tenants"]))

        raise AssertionError("The received collection did not retain its full original file set.")
    tenant = catalog["tenants"][original_tenant]
    required_files = []
    for expected in expected_companions:
        path = extracted / tenant["root"] / expected["path"]
        if path.stat().st_size != expected["bytes"] or file_sha(path) != expected["sha256"]:
            raise AssertionError("A declared original companion was omitted or changed during transfer.")
        primary = next(row for row in tenant["datasets"] if row["id"] == expected["primary_id"])
        retained = [item for item in primary["metadata"]["retained_companions"]
                    if item.get("source_dataset_id") == expected["source_dataset_id"]]
        if len(retained) != 1 or any(retained[0].get(field) != expected[field]
                                     for field in ("path", "bytes", "sha256")):
            raise AssertionError("The received companion lost its original dataset identity.")

        continuation = state_directory / "reexported-original-collection"
        continued = bundle(catalog, extracted, continuation,
                           [{"tenant_id": original_tenant, **ref} for ref in refs])
        portable_continuation = verify_delivery(continuation)
        if (continued["selected_records"] != len({json.dumps(ref, sort_keys=True) for ref in refs})
                or continued["files"] != json.loads(
                    (extracted / "delivery.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["files"]):
            raise AssertionError("Portable continuation changed selected records or their required originals.")

    operator = Operator(workspace, state_directory)
    try:
        key, feature = operator.primary, controller(operator)
        reopened = feature.read(key, "collection", {
            "session_id": sid, "collection_id": collection_id})
        new_ticket = next(item for item in reopened["files"] if item["format"] == "zip")
        if (new_ticket["id"], new_ticket["sha256"], reopened["catalog_sha256"]) != (
                ticket["id"], ticket["sha256"], original_view["catalog_sha256"]):
            raise AssertionError("Restart changed the retained collection identity.")
        resumed = operator.submit(key, "intelligence.collection.export", payload, export_op)
        if resumed["id"] != exported["id"] or resumed["result"]["collection_id"] != collection_id:
            raise AssertionError("Restart replay changed the original collection.")
        decorated = operator.task_view(exported["id"])
        if not any(row["id"] == new_ticket["id"] for row in decorated.get("_downloads", [])):
            raise AssertionError("The original task did not reopen its collection download.")
        original_file, _ = operator.open_download(new_ticket["id"])
        original_file.close()
        result = {"status": "passed", "project_id": project,
                  "workspace_key": key, "session_id": sid, "task_id": exported["id"],
                  "collection_id": collection_id, "selected_original_refs": refs,
                  "zip": {"bytes": ticket["bytes"], "sha256": ticket["sha256"]},
                  "received": received, "reopened_files": reopened_files,
                  "declared_companions": required_files,
                  "portable_companion_continuation": portable_continuation,
                  "replay_same_task": True, "restart_same_collection": True,
                  "native_task_download_reopened": True}
        (state_directory / "collection-receiving-result.json").write_text(
            json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        return result
    finally:
        operator.close()

# Original county sources to an editable GIS handover

The **Original map layers** desk now opens the existing **Editable GIS projects**
desk with the admitted county vector, its original attribute table and the dated
Census context selected together. Choose **Prepare complete editable GIS handover**
on a saved admission. The GIS desk refreshes its authoritative source catalogue
before displaying these exact original source IDs.

The display coordinate system starts at EPSG:4326 for these admitted sources.
Working files keep their native coordinates. The form retains ordinary GIS
choices: source files, optional prepared grids and completed native results,
display projection and operator notes. Use **Build complete GIS project** to
submit the original `gis.project.export` operation.

## What travels with the handover

The complete ZIP contains its QGIS project, independently editable working
GeoPackage, original vector and every declared companion. This includes the
full original Web Map, its extracted Esri feature set and geometry provenance.
The original attribute table and Census table are retained as typed table
attachments with all their companions, including the county crosswalk, dated
metadata, original feature join and readable population report.

The project manifest also preserves explicit scientific source metadata:
original collection/source identity, parent lineage, original field definitions
and vintages, and the dated table's geography and column metadata. The population
table describes whole counties. These values remain separate from clipped model
geographies and retain their original Census estimate vintage and date.

The existing GIS receive and adoption workflow supports continued work. Receiving
a complete archive creates an independent edition. Adopting its working layer
creates a new native source collection with the associated originals and context.
Re-exporting that working layer automatically includes its retained context.
The adopted CSVs remain native tables. Their original format, columns, per-column
scientific metadata, declared units and conversion, source date, geography and
provenance remain available to the ordinary source catalogue and table profiler.
Each adopted table also retains the exact original collection/source binding and
ordered primary/companion identities under its received GIS provenance.

## Continue the original receiving operation

Use the installed maintained application and its actual GIS interpreter. The
original publisher Workspace is project
`c6095eb6-b080-42e5-b89e-0d36accb98f4`. It contains the original ten-county
publisher source. Add the GIS state argument to the existing admission command:

```bash
"$ACTUAL_GIS_PYTHON" -B "$ACTUAL_APP/source_tools/receive_webmap_sources.py" \
  --application "$ACTUAL_APP" --workspace "$ACTUAL_ORIGINAL_WORKSPACE" \
  --state-directory "$ACTUAL_ADMISSION_STATE" \
  --collection-receiver "$ACTUAL_APP/receiving/eco_intelligence/receive_original_collection.py" \
  --collection-state-directory "$ACTUAL_COLLECTION_STATE" \
  --gis-state-directory "$ACTUAL_GIS_STATE"
```

Use a distinct GIS operator state directory. Existing admitted originals are
reused. The optional GIS phase runs after the existing admission and selected
collection procedures have closed their Operators.

For an admission already received, its native source collection ID can be passed
directly:

```bash
"$ACTUAL_GIS_PYTHON" -B "$ACTUAL_APP/source_tools/receive_webmap_gis.py" \
  --application "$ACTUAL_APP" --workspace "$ACTUAL_ORIGINAL_WORKSPACE" \
  --source-collection-id "$ACTUAL_ADMITTED_COLLECTION" \
  --state-directory "$ACTUAL_GIS_STATE"
```

The GIS receiver uses the original queue for export, independent receive,
adoption, re-export and a second independent receive. It validates all ten
county identities, attributes and polygons through the native GeoPackage field
mapping and original county-name binding, checks the source/companion bindings, and verifies that the original
context travels when only the adopted working layer is selected. It also opens
both adopted CSVs through the actual native table profiler, checks all ten rows
against their retained originals, and verifies typed metadata and every declared
companion through re-export. It then
restarts the Operator and reopens the same tasks, source collection, typed table
profiles and archive downloads.

## Resume and use the resulting project

Rerun the same command and GIS version with the same state directory to continue
the recorded original tasks. Interrupted, failed or cancelled tasks are resumed through
`Operator.resume`; completed tasks retain their original IDs and selections.
The state record names the original accepted tasks even when the native queue
coalesced an identical active request.

`webmap-gis-receiving-result.json` records the original source identity, both
receiving fingerprints, the adopted collection, native task IDs and the final
complete ZIP's retained path, length and SHA-256. Its final status becomes
`passed` after the restart and download reopening finish. Each exported and
received edition also appears in the existing GIS desk. Open the layer view or
download the complete ZIP there, then open `project.qgz` in QGIS.


## Receiving earlier GIS editions

GIS builder and adopter version 1.3.0 records explicit attachment types and uses
a distinct scientific source adoption identity. Existing version 1.2 exports can
also be adopted: their retained original request supplies the table type only
after its logical ID, original source metadata and ordered primary/companion
paths, lengths and hashes match the received attachment. File extensions never
determine the scientific source kind.

A source edition already adopted with the earlier document-only behavior remains
unchanged. Running a new adoption uses the current adopter version and produces
a separate typed source edition. The receiving driver records the GIS version
with its original operation identity. Use a separate GIS state directory when
advancing an already completed earlier-version receiving run; its original task
records and deliveries remain available.

Physical files can be shared by several retained logical sources. Context
identity includes its original role, logical source ID, explicit type, metadata
and ordered file bindings, so a generic layer original cannot suppress a typed
table that happens to use the same bytes. Selecting an adopted working layer
continues to carry every required table, document, original file and companion.


## Use the offline source desk

Open `OPEN_GIS.html` directly from the extracted GIS directory and choose
**Sources and tables**. This is the same offline opener as the retained map;
the original layer controls, legends and geographic view remain available under
**Layers**.

The source list includes every layer's original files and every typed table or
document attachment. Search the original title, date, scientific metadata or
filename. Select the Census context to see its original estimate vintage,
whole-county geography, units and column definitions beside the literal rows.
Leading-zero identifiers and empty values remain unchanged. Row search and
pagination work inside the extracted file; clicking a column sorts its displayed
values as text, and **Original row order** restores their source order.

Each source exposes its primary download and every declared companion. These
include the exact original Web Map, extracted features, historical attributes,
geometry provenance, Census metadata, crosswalk, original-feature join and
readable population report. The editable working layer has its own download.

The catalogue embeds complete county tables. For other large sources it embeds
up to 2,000 display rows within a one-million-character display budget, and states
whether the entire table is displayed. Search and sort apply to those displayed
rows. The full original table and all companions always remain in the handover.

**Save this view** retains the selected source or layer, table search, text sort,
page, visible layers and map extent. The view address carries the same selection.
It is bound to the exact GIS selection and edition, so a saved view cannot apply
a source selection from another project edition. Browser storage is optional;
the view address supports reopening when local storage is unavailable.

The original receiving driver checks the embedded offline table values against
both complete ten-row source CSVs before and after native adoption and
working-layer-only re-export. This joins the human-readable opener to the same
typed scientific sources and companion identities checked by the native flow.


## Reuse an original table or document without a working layer

Open **Editable GIS projects → Received independent editions → Use received layers, tables or documents as study sources**. Clear the working-layer selections, then select the original tables or documents you need. Each choice shows its retained kind, date, geography, declared units and number of companions. Give the new source edition a title and reason, then submit through the normal Operations queue.

The new edition uses the original source importer. A selected CSV remains a table with its exact original header, values, primary bytes, ordered companions, URI, vintage, units and scientific metadata. A selected document remains a document. The source record retains the received GIS edition, original source binding and adoption reason. An additional provenance document carries the received project manifest and retained edition history. This mode does not require a vector or raster.

The selected table is directly selectable in the ordinary Sources and Investigations catalogues. **Open original source files** in the GIS desk opens that saved edition through the existing source-item API and refreshes download tickets for every primary and companion. The completed adoption task also links the original source edition and its files. Adoption form selections and the original queue operation ID survive a page reload; a changed selection gets its own operation.

If any working layer is selected, every original context attachment stays selected and is carried with that layer, preserving the existing layer-only re-export behavior. To choose a subset of tables or documents, clear all working layers first. Empty selections, repeated identities and identities absent from the received edition are rejected.

### Native request

The existing action is `gis.project.adopt-sources`:

```json
{
  "receipt_id": "<actual saved receiving ID>",
  "title": "Dated county population source",
  "reason": "Reuse the original whole-county table in this study.",
  "layer_ids": [],
  "attachment_ids": ["<actual attachment ID from the received catalogue>"]
}
```

`GISProjects.catalogue(workspace_key)` returns both `layer_choices` and `attachment_choices` for each received edition. Copy the exact attachment identity. A request with working layers and no `attachment_ids` retains every attachment, as earlier clients expect. When explicit attachment IDs accompany working layers, they must include the complete attachment set.

The immutable adoption selection includes `adoption_format_version: 2`, the original receiving fingerprint, ordered selected IDs and the existing GIS builder version. Earlier cached layer-only adoptions remain intact. The result retains `sources` for working-layer mappings and adds `context_sources` with attachment ID, native source ID, title and kind.

### Continue the original county receiving course

The same `source_tools/receive_webmap_gis.py` now continues through independent table adoption. It checks the actual catalogue choice, admits the original dated Census CSV without working geometry, verifies all original metadata/companions and the complete native profile, and opens the completed native task's source downloads. It then selects the adopted originals and received-edition provenance using the actual Investigations repository references and delegates to the maintained `receiving/eco_intelligence/receive_original_collection.py` for its original export, companion checks, portable re-export and restart/reopen.

This receiver uses `receiving_version: typed-source-selection-v2` and a separate `source-only-collection` state directory beneath the same receiving operation. Preserve any active earlier receiver and its task state. Run the maintained continuation only after that original lifetime is reconciled; use a new state directory for a different receiving/GIS version. The saved result reports `source_only_collection_id`, `source_only_tables`, `source_only_refs` and `source_only_collection_export` alongside the original full GIS course.


## Review received vector edits before source adoption

Each received GIS edition with vector layers now has **Review all vector layers** in the existing Editable GIS desk. This queues `gis.vector.review` through the original Operations queue. The received edition and explicit layer IDs determine the immutable review identity. Retrying the same request reopens the original task and result.

The completed review appears beside that same received edition and source-adoption form. Open it to inspect the original and working CRS, exact paired-feature counts, attribute changes, geometry changes, unresolved identities, and full original source context. Complete JSON, CSV, HTML and a self-contained ZIP use the existing authenticated download tickets. Extract the ZIP and open `review.html` to read every feature offline.

### What the comparison means

The comparison uses the retained original primary and every declared companion, with their exact path, byte length and SHA256. It resolves the original source layer and original selection from `source_request`, and validates the saved `source_field_map` and `source_identity_field`. Feature order and desktop GeoPackage row numbers are not used to infer a match.

A feature with one exact original identity on each side is compared field by field. Literal identifiers, empty strings, nulls and zero values remain distinct. Added and removed fields are shown, and field-type changes remain explicit in the layer schema. An identity appearing only on one side is reported as an added or removed **identity**: editing an ID can produce the same observation as adding or removing a feature. When working IDs are absent, unmatched original features are reported without assuming deletion. Duplicate IDs are shown as ambiguous groups with every original and working feature.

XY geometry uses Shapely topological equality in equivalent declared CRSs, so changing a polygon's ring order alone does not create a spatial edit. Geometry type and Z coordinate changes are recorded separately in the equality result; Z comparison retains the complete coordinate multiset. Measured M coordinates, invalid geometry or differing CRSs produce an explicit unassessed comparison. The review does not repair geometry, reproject it implicitly, convert areas, or derive scientific impact from a desktop edit.

The baseline is the complete retained original source selection. A sealed edition retains previous project metadata and file hashes, but does not retain all former working geometry bodies; the report therefore does not describe a previous editable edition as its baseline.

After reviewing the result, the existing source-adoption form creates a separate native source collection from that exact received edition. The review and adoption remain independently retained and share the original receipt/edition identity. Working layers carry their complete original context as before; original tables and documents can also be adopted separately.

### Native receiving and workspace restore

The existing `source_tools/receive_webmap_gis.py` course now queues the review for its actual, unchanged ten-county received vector, requires ten exact original matches with unchanged attributes and geometry, opens all four original task downloads, and checks the same retained review after Operator restart. Its prior GIS, typed-table, source-only adoption and selected-source collection phases are unchanged.

Review files live under `gis-vector-reviews/<selection-id>/` in the original Workspace. The current portable backup recursively retains that directory and the new model/operator/descriptor files. The extension's original `verify_workspace` callback verifies the review's project, received edition, complete files and full report when restoring. Download tickets are regenerated for the receiving workspace key.

The new component is installed with the normal application source cohort:

- `model/gis_vector_review.py`
- `operator/gis_vector_reviews.py`
- `operator/extensions/gis-vector-reviews.json`
- the complete current `operator/web/gis-projects.mjs`

There is no new parallel GIS workspace, task queue, archive format or scientific solver.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Receive saved source-review decisions through the original queue and uploads."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from copy import deepcopy
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys
import time


def receive(application, workspace, state_directory, *, review_id=None, decisions_path=None, timeout=240):
    application, workspace = Path(application).resolve(), Path(workspace).resolve()
    state_directory = Path(state_directory).resolve()
    state_directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    sys.path[:0] = [str(application / "operator"), str(application)]
    from server import Operator, Fault
    from gis_review_decisions import GISReviewDecisions
    from model import gis_project as gis, gis_vector_review, gis_review_decisions
    from model.common import atomic_json, digest

    operator = Operator(workspace, state_directory)
    journal_path = state_directory / "source-review-decisions-receiving.json"
    try:
        key, feature = operator.primary, GISReviewDecisions(operator, Fault)
        ws = operator.ws(key)
        retained = json.loads(journal_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if journal_path.is_file() else None
        if retained:
            selected = retained["identity"]["review_id"]
            if review_id is not None and review_id != selected:
                raise ValueError("Use the retained original review or a separate receiving state.")
            review_id = selected
        if not review_id:
            choices = gis_vector_review.catalog(ws)
            if not choices:
                raise ValueError("Complete the original-source GIS vector review before receiving decisions.")
            review_id = choices[0]["id"]
        ref = gis_review_decisions.reference(ws, review_id)
        identity = {"project_id": ws.project["id"], "review_id": review_id,
                    "comparison_sha256": ref["comparison_sha256"],
                    "receiving_version": "source-review-decisions-v1"}
        if retained:
            if retained.get("identity") != identity:
                raise ValueError("The receiving journal belongs to another original comparison.")
            receipt = retained
        else:
            receipt = {"schema": "upstate.gis-review-decisions-receiving/v1",
                       "identity": identity, "phases": {}}
            atomic_json(journal_path, receipt)

        if decisions_path:
            requested = json.loads(Path(decisions_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            if requested.get("review_id") != review_id:
                raise ValueError("The requested decisions belong to another original review.")
            original_payload = requested
        elif receipt.get("original_payload"):
            original_payload = receipt["original_payload"]
        else:
            selected = next((row for row in ref["rows"]
                             if row["comparison"]["status"] != "layer_definition"), ref["rows"][0])
            original_payload = {"review_id": review_id, "previous_id": None,
                "title": "Source review receiving", "reviewer": "",
                "decisions": [{"key": selected["key"], "disposition": "unreviewed",
                    "note": "Original comparison opened for source transfer and review.\n"
                            "This note records receiving continuity; the review disposition remains open."}]}
        if receipt.get("original_payload", original_payload) != original_payload:
            raise ValueError("The retained receiving request changed. Preserve it and use another state for new decisions.")
        receipt["original_payload"] = deepcopy(original_payload)
        atomic_json(journal_path, receipt)

        def complete(phase, action, payload):
            request = {"workspace": key, "action": action, "payload": payload}
            operation = "eco264b-decisions-" + digest(identity)[:16] + "-" + phase
            previous = receipt["phases"].get(phase)
            if previous:
                if previous["request"] != request:
                    raise ValueError("The original decision operation changed selection.")
                task = operator.task(previous["task_id"])
            else:
                task = operator.submit(key, action, payload, operation)
                if any(task.get(name) != value for name, value in request.items()):
                    raise ValueError("The native queue returned another original decision request.")
                receipt["phases"][phase] = {"request": request, "task_id": task["id"],
                                            "operation_id": task["operation_id"]}
                atomic_json(journal_path, receipt)
            if (any(task.get(name) != value for name, value in request.items())
                    or task["operation_id"] != receipt["phases"][phase]["operation_id"]):
                raise ValueError("The retained native task changed its accepted original identity.")
            if task["state"] in {"failed", "cancelled", "interrupted"}:
                task = operator.resume(task["id"])
            deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
            while task["state"] in {"queued", "running"}:
                if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                    raise TimeoutError("The original review operation remains active: " + task["id"])
                time.sleep(.1)
                task = operator.task(task["id"])
            if task["state"] != "complete":
                raise RuntimeError(json.dumps(task, ensure_ascii=False))
            receipt["phases"][phase]["result_id"] = task["result"]["id"]
            atomic_json(journal_path, receipt)
            return task

        def opened(task):
            value = feature.read(key, "inspect", {"id": task["result"]["id"]})
            if value["comparison_sha256"] != identity["comparison_sha256"]:
                raise AssertionError("The retained decision result changed its scientific comparison.")
            return value

        def upload_ticket(value, filename):
            candidates = [row for row in value["_downloads"] if row["filename"] == filename]
            if len(candidates) != 1:
                raise AssertionError("The complete native review download is missing: " + filename)
            ticket = candidates[0]
            stream, _ = operator.open_download(ticket["id"])
            try:
                upload = operator.receive_upload(stream, ticket["bytes"], ticket["filename"],
                                                  "application/zip" if filename.endswith(".zip") else "application/json")

            raise AssertionError("Saving changed the original review notes or dispositions.")
